data.title: Justin Sun says Tron’s post-quantum cryptography has gone live on testnet
data.description:
Justin Sun, founder of the Tron network, said that the company’s post-quantum cryptography was now live on testnet.

“We’re closely tracking progress in quantum computing and AI, and we’re ready to bring quantum resistance to mainnet at any time, Sun said in a post on X on Saturday.

He added, “We’re committed to keeping user assets secure, and TRON is set to be one of the few major blockchains that is quantum-resistant before Q-Day,” or the day when quantum computing becomes capable of breaking current security standards.

Coindesk reported on July 28 that Blockchain security company AmericanFortress had unveiled a cryptographic plan to protect crypto wallets from future quantum attacks without requiring users to move funds, rotate keys or change wallet addresses.

Unlike most proposed post-quantum approaches, AmericanFortress said it allows existing wallet addresses to remain unchanged while adding post-quantum protection.

Proposal published in technical paper

The company published the proposal in a technical paper on the Cryptography ePrint Archive, though it had not yet been peer-reviewed.

Developers have increasingly focused on post-quantum cryptography because sufficiently powerful quantum computers may eventually break the elliptic-curve cryptography used to secure Bitcoin, Ethereum and many other blockchain networks

Earlier this year, a Strategy-led consortium pledged $15 million to fund Bitcoin quantum security research, the Ethereum Foundation published a proposal for migrating accounts to quantum-resistant cryptography and Algorand outlined plans to introduce quantum-resistant accounts by 2027.

data.title: Sweep-in FD vs regular FD: 5 key differences investors should know
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- A sweep-in fixed deposit (FD) is an investment option that helps bank customers earn interest on surplus savings. All the while retaining access to their funds to meet unexpected expenses such as a medical emergency, unforeseen surgery, an accident, or home renovation expenses.

A regular FD, by contrast, permits investors to deposit a lump sum amount for a chosen tenure. Both these investment options can offer better returns than a savings account; still, their liquidity, withdrawal and redemption rules and interest calculations differ.

That is why, before opting to proceed with any of these options, aspiring investors should understand the basic differences between them and compare banks' interest rates, minimum-balance requirements, and premature withdrawal conditions.

A sweep-in FD generally earns the applicable interest rate of a regular FD for the corresponding tenure. However, premature withdrawals may attract penalties or different interest calculations.

For instance, SBI's regular FD rates broadly range from 3.05% to 6.40% p.a., depending on tenure, with sweep-in returns subject to deposit terms. Keeping these basics in mind, let us discuss the core difference between the two. Such an approach will assist aspiring investors with meaningful financial planning.

Note: The salient features and differences discussed above are illustrative. For a complete understanding of specific fixed deposits, refer to the official website of the respective lender.

State Bank of India: Investors can invest in the State Bank of India (SBI) Multi-Option Deposit Scheme (MODS). This scheme supports auto-sweep. Currently, the published minimum auto-sweep threshold is Rs.50,000, with a minimum resulting savings-account balance of Rs.35,000. Deposits under this start as Rs.15,000 in multiples of Rs.5,000, whereas reverse-sweep withdrawals are made in Rs.5,000 units. The rules discussed here are illustrative and subject to change per bank policy. Hence, proper due diligence is a must before considering any investments.

HDFC Bank: Its FD terms specify that premature withdrawals, including sweep-in and partial withdrawals, may attract a 1% reduction in the applicable interest rate. These rules are not fixed; they are tentative and subject to the kind of fixed deposit invested and the bank's policies. Furthermore, linked-account balance requirements and service charges also continue to apply.

ICICI Bank: Effective 5 October 2026, ICICI Bank's fixed deposits (FDs) go up to 6.50% for general customers and 7.10% for senior citizens on eligible tenures. This is a broad range of FD rates and does not guarantee identical effective returns for every sweep-in transaction.

It is essential to keep in mind that sweep-in FDs generally follow the bank's applicable FD rate structure, but actual returns differ when funds are withdrawn early. That is why it is wise to check each bank's current applicable rate card and investment terms before considering any investment.

There cannot be a single answer to this question. As investments are need-based and done according to an individual's financial reality and long-term economic objectives. The investment decision, hence, should be based on how one intends to use their funds.

A sweep-in FD may suit people who want to earn FD interest on surplus funds while retaining convenient access to cash. A regular FD may be more appropriate for money earmarked for a specific goal.

In case of doubt or hesitation, it is wise to seek help from a certified financial advisor before making any investments, as this approach ensures your investments are guided by professionals and made appropriately in line with your long-term financial objectives.

data.title: Hurricane Isaias Makes Landfall in Florida — WSJ
data.description:
By Joseph Pisani

Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Fla., Friday night, bringing heavy rains, damaging winds and the possibility of life-threatening flooding to the region.

"Buckle down at this point," Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said. "Don't be getting out on the roads."

The Category 2 hurricane hit the U.S. Gulf Coast around 9:30 p.m. Eastern time with 105 mph winds, pulling out trees and knocking down power lines before grinding north through Alabama.

More than 700,000 customers in Alabama and Florida were without power early Saturday, according to PowerOutage.com, which tracks outages. Utility companies said they would send out crews to make repairs when it was safe to do so.

"Residents in these areas should have a safe room to ride out the storm and prepare for long-duration power outages," the National Weather Service said.

Forecasters had discontinued storm-surge warnings by 4 a.m. Saturday but said flash, urban and river flooding remained a threat.

As much as 8 inches of rainfall is expected this weekend in southern Alabama, the Florida Panhandle and southwest Georgia, the weather service said.

The hurricane is expected to weaken as it moves inland Saturday, "but Isaias is expected to continue producing gusty winds well inland," the National Weather Service said.

Isaias is the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 in what has been a relatively quiet season.

data.title: Jio Platforms IPO: How Reliance boss Mukesh Ambani's mega issue compares with India's 5 biggest IPOs - price, valuation
data.description:
Reliance Jio IPO, Oct. 10 -- Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms is preparing for a mega initial public offering (IPO) that could rank among India's largest public issues by fundraising. With a reported price band of Rs.1,065 to Rs.1,119 per share, the offering is expected to raise up to Rs.30,213 crore and value the company at as much as Rs.10.3 lakh crore, or approximately $106 billion.

With this, Jio IPO is on track to dethrone Hyundai Motor India Limited to become India's largest-ever IPO.

Key dates: The proposed IPO involves up to 27 crore fresh equity shares, with no Offer for Sale (OFS) component from existing institutional shareholders, according to the details provided. The issue is expected to open for anchor investors on October 19, 2026, followed by the public subscription period from October 21 to October 23.

Jio Platforms IPO last recorded Grey Market Premium (GMP) was Rs.172, as on Oct 10, 2026. With a reported upper price band of Rs.1,119, its listing price is estimated to be 1291, indicating a listing premium of 15.4% from IPO price.

Jio Platforms' proposed fundraising puts it alongside some of India's largest IPOs, including Hyundai Motor India, the National Stock Exchange (NSE), Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), Paytm's parent One97 Communications and Tata Capital.

Hyundai Motor India set a record for India's largest IPO when it went public in October 2024. The company launched its issue at a price band of Rs.1,865 to Rs.1,960 per share and raised Rs.27,858.75 crore.

The IPO was entirely an Offer for Sale, allowing Hyundai Motor India's South Korean parent to sell 14.22 crore shares to investors. Unlike Jio Platforms' proposed fresh issue, the Hyundai offering was designed to provide an exit opportunity for the existing shareholder rather than raise fresh capital for the company.

Hyundai Motor India commanded a listing-day market valuation of more than Rs.1.5 lakh crore.

The National Stock Exchange (NSE) launched its public issue in September 2026, with a reference price of Rs.1,785 per share and a total issue size of Rs.22,562.71 crore. NSE IPO bidding started from Sep 17, 2026 and ended on Sep 21, 2026.

The offering was structured entirely as an OFS, providing an exit opportunity for existing institutional shareholders while meeting the relevant regulatory requirements. The exchange was valued at approximately $46 billion, placing the issue among India's largest public offerings. The public issue was oversubscribed 4.26 times overall, generating total bids for over 53.80 crore shares against the 12.64 crore shares on offer

Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) went public in May 2022 in one of the country's most closely watched divestment exercises. The government offered shares at Rs.902 to Rs.949 apiece and raised Rs.20,557.23 crore by selling a 3.5% stake through an OFS of 22.14 crore shares.

The IPO also included discounts for eligible investors, with retail buyers receiving a Rs.45 discount and policyholders receiving a Rs.60 discount.

The IPO garnered an overall subscription of 2.95 times, with strong participation from policyholders and employees, who were also offered special discounts. The transaction was closely watched globally as it represented one of the largest government-led stake sales in the country's capital market history.

One97 Communications, the parent company of Paytm, entered the public markets in November 2021 with an IPO worth Rs.18,300 crore. The issue had a price band of Rs.2,080 to Rs.2,150 per share.

The offering combined a fresh issue of Rs.8,300 crore with an OFS of Rs.10,000 crore. At the upper end of the price band, Paytm's initial market valuation stood at Rs.1.01 lakh crore.

The issue reflected investor interest in India's digital payments and fintech businesses during a period of expansion for the sector. The IPO was subscribed 1.89 times, supported by participation from institutional and retail investors. At the time, it was India's largest-ever IPO and marked a milestone for the country's rapidly expanding fintech sector.

Tata Capital entered the public market in October 2025 with an issue size of Rs.15,511.87 crore. The non-banking financial company used a price cap of Rs.326 per share. The issue was open for subscription from October 6 to October 8, 2025, and the shares were listed on October 13, 2025. The issue is a combination of fresh issue of 21.00 crore shares aggregating to Rs.6,846.00 crores and offer for sale of 26.58 crore shares aggregating to Rs.8,665.87 crores.

The IPO brought the Tata group's financial services business to the public markets while combining fundraising for the company with a secondary stake sale.

The company fixed a price band of Rs.310 to Rs.326 per share. Backed by the strong Tata brand and investor interest in financial services companies, the IPO closed with an overall subscription of 1.95 times. The listing further strengthened the Tata Group's already significant presence in India's equity markets.

data.title: Swedish Tax Agency requires security for deferral of payment in transfer pricing case 2019-2022 – Valuno appeals
data.description:
Valuno Group AB (publ) (the "Company") received the Swedish Tax Agency's response on the deferral of payment relating to the previously announced transfer pricing decision for the years 2019-2022. The Swedish Tax Agency considers that a deferral of payment may be granted but requires the Company to provide security in the form of a bank guarantee for the income tax of SEK 23,430,747 and interest by 2 November 2026. For the tax surcharges of SEK 20,681,284, a deferral of payment is granted without security.

The Company does not share the Swedish Tax Agency's assessment and will appeal the security requirement to the Administrative Court in Stockholm, requesting a deferral of payment without security.

At the same time, the Swedish Tax Agency has granted the Company a temporary deferral of payment from 12 October to 12 November 2026, pending final determination of the question of security. The amount therefore does not fall due for payment on 12 October 2026 and is not referred for enforcement during the deferral period.

On 4 September 2026, the Company announced the Swedish Tax Agency's final decision in the transfer pricing case, which rests on the view that the parent company, and not the Gibraltar subsidiary QuickBit Ltd, performed the value creating functions and controlled the significant risks relating to the group's affiliate solution. That decision was appealed on 29 September 2026.

“The response was expected. We do not share the Swedish Tax Agency's assessment and will appeal the security requirement to the Administrative Court”, says Peter Liljeroos, CEO of Valuno Group AB (publ).

data.title: Bitcoin's $19 billion crash still shapes crypto risk a year later
data.description:
One year ago, a single tariff announcement erased more than $19 billion in leveraged crypto bets in about a day. It remains the largest derivatives liquidation episode the market has ever recorded.

The trigger came from Washington, not from inside crypto. President Donald Trump announced a 100% tariff on Chinese imports, and markets that had been priced for good news suddenly had to reprice for a trade war.

Crypto derivatives took the hit fastest. Forced liquidations topped $19 billion across exchanges within a 24-hour window.

The damage reached over 1.6 million accounts. Most of the pain fell on traders betting prices would rise: long positions made up roughly $16–17 billion of the total.

Bitcoin had set an all-time high of nearly $126,200 just four days earlier, on October 6. During the crash, it fell somewhere between 14% and 17% intraday, touching lows in the range of $102,000 to $107,000 before clawing some of it back.

Open interest, the total value of outstanding derivatives contracts, dropped by more than 30% during the selloff. Across the broader crypto market, hundreds of billions in market capitalization vanished within hours.

Binance offered $300 million in compensation to users affected by its automated liquidation process during the volatility.

The crash also exposed structural weak points in how crypto derivatives work. Two stood out: thin liquidity and cross-margin mechanics.

Thin liquidity means there were not enough buyers waiting to absorb the flood of forced selling. Prices gapped down rather than sliding.

Cross-margin is a setup where a trader's whole account balance backs all of their open positions. In a crash, one losing trade can drain collateral that was supporting everything else, turning a single bad bet into a full account wipeout.

On-chain analyses put the realized losses for traders far below $19 billion, with estimates ranging from $950 million to $2.85 billion. The gap exists because the $19 billion reflects the notional size of positions that were closed, not the cash traders actually lost.

Metaplanet reported that its profits fell 39% in Q3, a sign of how the 10/10 event rippled through companies that hold Bitcoin on their balance sheets.

As of early October 2026, Bitcoin trades around $83,000 to $83,500, roughly 34% below its peak.

The liquidation event did flush a large amount of leverage out of the system. But positioning in the months afterward indicated traders had not meaningfully scaled back their appetite for risk. Leverage monitoring around the anniversary shows only modest easing in risk metrics.

For individual traders, the clearest takeaway is about tail risk. The 10/10 crash was set off by a policy announcement from outside the crypto ecosystem. No on-chain metric would have flagged it in advance, and leveraged longs had no time to react before automated systems acted for them.

For exchanges, the episode raised the bar on transparency. Binance's $300 million compensation offer showed that how a platform handles automated liquidations in extreme conditions is a reputational issue, not just a technical one.

A crash that hit over 1.6 million accounts in a single day may push some newcomers toward spot holdings or more conservative strategies, and it could keep others away from derivatives entirely.

Open interest, funding conditions, and the share of positions using cross-margin are the gauges to track. When those climb back toward pre-crash levels while liquidity stays thin, the market is effectively rebuilding the same dominoes that fell on October 10.

data.title: Have leftover money on your forex card after a foreign trip? Here's how to transfer it back to your Indian bank account
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- When a Indian resident travels abroad, they generally carry a forex card to pay for expenses such as accommodation, transport, food and experiences. However, it is not necessary to spend the card's entire balance during the trip, which means travellers may return to India with money left on their forex card.

This unused balance can be converted into Indian rupees (INR) through the card issuer's refund or encashment process. The applicable process, exchange rate, charges, and refund method may may vary across forex card issuers.

The INR amount you receive depends on the foreign currency balance and the exchange rate applicable at the time of encashment. Any applicable encashment or conversion charges may be deducted from the final amount.

For example, if you have $1,000 remaining on your forex card and the applicable exchange rate is Rs.96 per US dollar, the gross value of the balance would be Rs.96,000 before deducting any applicable charges and taxes.

According to a report by Paisabazaar, some forex card issuers allow travellers to transfer the leftover money in their forex card to their bank account in Indian rupees. Though the facility and process may vary depending on the issuer, the process can look like this:

Step 1: Log in to the forex card issuer's mobile app or online portal.

Step 2: Navigate to the forex card section and select the option for refund or encashment.

Step 3: Select the currency and amount you want to refund. You can also choose the option to refund the entire balance if it's available.

Step 4: Select the bank account where you want the refund to be credited.

Step 5: Check the applicable exchange rate at the time, additional charges, as well as terms and conditions before proceeding.

Step 6: Submit the refund request and complete any required verification.

Once your request is processed, the remaining forex card's balance will be converted into Indian rupees and credited to the selected bank account.

A customer can also visit the forex card issuer's nearest branch with the required documents to submit a refund or encashment request form.

data.title: Cohance Lifesciences Appoints Abhimanyu Ojha As CFO
data.description:
Former Intas Pharmaceuticals global CFO takes charge on 12 October as Cohance navigates revenue pressure and planned investments in antibody-drug conjugates

Cohance Lifesciences has appointed Abhimanyu Ojha as Chief Financial Officer (CFO), effective 12 October 2026, filling the position following Himanshu Agarwal’s departure in September. Ojha brings more than two decades of financial leadership experience in the global healthcare and pharmaceutical sectors, having previously served as Global CFO of Intas Pharmaceuticals.

The appointment comes as Cohance navigates a challenging financial period and pursues investments to expand its capabilities in antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), a specialised segment of pharmaceutical development and manufacturing. Ojha’s responsibilities will include overseeing the company’s financial operations and supporting capital allocation decisions as it executes its growth strategy.

Previous CFO Departure

Agarwal resigned from the CFO position in June 2026 and was relieved of his responsibilities on 13 September 2026. Ojha’s appointment formalises the leadership transition at a time when the company is working to strengthen its position in contract development and manufacturing services.

The transition follows the appointment of Umang Vohra, former Cipla chief, as Executive Chairman and Group CEO in April 2026. Vohra assumed the leadership role as Cohance continued to pursue its strategic priorities across complex pharmaceutical manufacturing.

Revenue Faces Pressure

Cohance reported revenue from operations of Rs 422.3 cr in the first quarter of FY27, a year-on-year decline of 23.1%. Gross margins also moderated to 71.5% from 73% in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.

The financial performance presents a key context for the incoming CFO, particularly in managing operating costs, margins and capital deployment. Future quarterly results will provide a clearer indication of the company’s revenue trajectory and operational performance.

ADC Investment Plans

In September 2026, Cohance announced plans to invest USD 13 million in NJ Bio and USD 5 million in Aruka Bio as part of its strategy to expand its ADC capabilities. The proposed investments are intended to strengthen its presence in specialised pharmaceutical development and manufacturing.

The company’s investment plans place capital allocation and the integration of new capabilities among the financial priorities under its incoming CFO. The execution and returns from these investments will be important considerations as the company expands in higher-value pharmaceutical segments.

Financial Priorities Ahead

Ojha takes charge amid a leadership transition, a decline in quarterly revenue and planned investments in specialised manufacturing capabilities. His experience in pharmaceutical finance will be relevant as Cohance balances expansion plans with operating performance and financial discipline.

The company’s subsequent financial results and progress on its investment commitments will help indicate how effectively it converts its strategic plans into sustainable business performance.

data.title: Alok Industries Exits Czech Textile Subsidiary Mileta In Rs 5.6 Cr Deal
data.description:
The divestment follows a December 2025 agreement with CRESCON and removes Mileta from Alok Industries’ subsidiary structure

Alok Industries has completed the sale of its entire stake in Czech textile manufacturer Mileta a.s. for EUR 558,825, equivalent to approximately Rs 5.6 crore. The company informed the stock exchanges on 9 October 2026 that Alok Industries International Limited, its step-down wholly owned subsidiary, had completed the transaction.

The sale follows a share purchase agreement signed on 16 December 2025 between Alok Industries International Limited and CRESCON a.s., a company incorporated in the Czech Republic.

Under the agreement, the subsidiary agreed to transfer its entire equity stake in Mileta to CRESCON. The December filing stated that the transaction was subject to customary closing conditions and that Mileta would cease to be a subsidiary of Alok Industries upon completion.

The latest disclosure confirms that the transaction has closed. CRESCON operates in residential and resort property development and does not belong to Alok Industries’ promoter group or group companies, according to the original filing.

Mileta's Financial Performance

Mileta manufactures textile fibres, fabrics and other textile products. Its operations also include yarn dyeing, chemical processing of fabrics and wholesale trade. The company operates facilities in Horice, which handles weaving and administration, and Cerny Dul, which undertakes processing activities in the Czech Republic.

Mileta contributed approximately 4.11 per cent to Alok Industries’ consolidated turnover in FY25, according to the December 2025 disclosure. The company reported sales of Rs 152.27 crore and a loss of Rs 49.63 crore for the year ended 31 March 2025, compared with sales of Rs 153.23 crore and a loss of Rs 28.53 crore in FY24.

Alok Industries’ FY26 annual report information shows that Mileta’s sales increased to Rs 189.62 crore, while its loss narrowed to Rs 5.92 crore. The figures indicate an improvement in the subsidiary’s reported financial performance before the completion of the divestment. However, the disclosures reviewed do not establish the reasons behind the sale or quantify its impact on Alok Industries’ future profitability and debt position.

Sale Ends Subsidiary Status

The transaction transfers Alok Industries International Limited’s entire equity stake in Mileta to CRESCON. With the sale complete, Mileta no longer forms part of Alok Industries’ subsidiary structure. The company’s disclosures confirm the transaction value and completion but do not specify how Alok Industries intends to use the proceeds. The effect of the disposal on the group’s consolidated financial position will depend on the accounting treatment and any related costs or adjustments.

data.title: S&P 500 at 10,000 or bust: New ETF offers investors all-or-nothing bet on the index
data.description:
By Christine Idzelis

A new ETF is a long-term leveraged bet on the popular stock index

It's becoming harder to draw the line between investing and gambling.

Wall Street has continued to blur the lines between investing and gambling with one recently launched exchange-traded fund.

Earlier this month, Roundhill Investments launched the Roundhill S&P 500 Target 10,000 2030 ETF XX. The ETF essentially offers investors the chance to take a long-term leveraged bet that the S&P 500 SPX will continue to climb.

Options contracts held by the fund may deliver a substantial payout if the S&P 500 is trading above 10,000 on Jan. 10, 2030, when the contracts expire.

If the index falls short, then the contracts will expire worthless. Although the outcome for the options is binary, investors don't necessarily need to hold the fund until the contracts expire.

ETFs that use derivatives like options to offer investors leveraged exposure to a given index, stock or asset have proliferated in recent years. But, as Roundhill CEO Dave Mazza pointed out, most of these products have catered to day traders, by employing leverage that resets daily.

Unlike the hundreds of leveraged and inverse ETFs that came before it, the new Roundhill ETF is designed as a long-term leveraged play on the direction of the S&P 500.

With the S&P 500 notching a new record high earlier this week after three straight years of double-digit gains, a target of just above 10,000 probably appears within reach to many. Achieving the target would require a compound annual growth rate of about 8%, according to MarketWatch calculations.

That's slightly higher than the long-term average: Going back to 1928, the S&P 500 has delivered a compounded price return of 6.4%, excluding dividends, Dow Jones Market Data showed.

Like prediction markets, the fund offers investors the chance to take a "binary bet" on a predetermined outcome, said Dave Nadig, president and director of research at ETF.com, in an interview. That's where the gambling aspect comes into play, he noted. But because the leverage is long term and the product is packaged in an ETF, it might seem less risky to potential buyers.

"It's a bizarre way to think about the markets. It's gamification," Nadig said.

How it works

Instead of using binary prediction-market contracts, the ETF will invest in leaps, or long-term equity anticipation securities. These are long-dated options contracts - a kind of long-term portfolio insurance that can also be used to speculate.

Shares of the Roundhill ETF should rise and fall based on the value of the option contracts that it holds. These contracts are linked to an ETF that tracks the S&P 500. As the S&P 500 rises toward 10,000, the value of these contracts will likely increase, along with their likelihood of delivering a payoff.

At the same time, the contracts will lose some of their value as time passes and their expiration dates approach. For longer-dated options, the process of time decay happens slowly. Time to expiration and the volatility of the underlying stock index are dynamics that will drive price action in the ETF.

As for how much investors should expect the ETF to move from day to day, Drew Pettit, CIO at Roundhill Investments, said the contracts currently leave the ETF with 5.5 times embedded leverage to the S&P 500.

The fund's early performance offers a more concrete picture. On Oct. 2, when the S&P 500 rose 0.7%, the ETF rose 7.4%. When the index fell by 0.5% on Thursday, the ETF fell 4.9%, FactSet data showed.

To reach 10,000, the S&P 500 would have to climb almost 29% from Thursday's closing level. Whether it gets there or not, the ride will likely be a bumpy one.

"This is a volatile investment," said Roundhill's Mazza. "For someone who is just looking for long-term equity-market returns, this strategy is not for them."

Akin to gambling

Leveraged ETFs are generally risky and take big swings. Still, they have exploded in number over the past couple years. Meanwhile, a growing number of more speculative products have helped to inspire a flurry of new ETF launches.

"From a cultural and marketing standpoint," much of the ETF industry's product development over the last year has been "highly speculative" or akin to gambling, Nadig said.

"People are actually trying to wedge gambling into every corner of the financial market right now," he said. "I'm very, very against using the financial markets to create binary speculative bets."

The value of an option is not just a function of its time to expiration, but also factors in the volatility of the underlying product and how close it is to the strike price, said Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers.

"The trick to options trading is, did the underlying move happen quickly enough to defeat your decay," Sosnick said.

During the years before the contracts it is holding expire, the Roundhill ETF's structure and volatility profile will likely attract day traders looking to make short-term bets on the S&P 500.

Investors also have the option of buying the long-dated options contracts themselves - but that would involve paying up-front premiums to buy the contracts, which could carry wide spreads, and ETFs offer a potentially more palatable vehicle. The long-term nature of the leverage will also spare traders from the intense volatility decay experienced from holding leveraged ETFs that see big price swings and that reset daily.

Michael DeStefano contributed.

-Christine Idzelis

data.title: Is Your Grown Child Pulling Away? These Are the Early Signs of Estrangement — WSJ
data.description:
By Elizabeth Bernstein

When I interview parents who are estranged from their adult children, many say: "My child cut me off out of the blue. I didn't see it coming."

Yet people who have gone "no contact" with their parents often tell me that this decision was their last resort — and a long time coming.

Why the disconnect?

Estrangement typically occurs on a continuum — and parents don't always recognize the signs, says Kristina Scharp, a communication professor at Rutgers University who studies the issue. Think of a scale from one to 10, where 10 is full contact between parent and child and one is none. In between, there is a slow pullback: fewer calls and visits, less access granted.

"It's a myth that estrangement is always all or nothing," Scharp says.

Scharp identified eight characteristics of estrangement, or areas in which adult children who are pulling away from their parents change their behaviors or feelings:

Communication quantity: They reduce the amount of contact. In a less-severe estrangement, they might call from time to time. In a more severe case, there is no contact.

Communication quality: They stop sharing meaningful or personal information. Instead of talking about their job or partner, for example, they might talk about the weather.

Physical distance: They move away or stay away. Some might remain in touch. Others move and don't tell their parents where they live.

Presence or absence of emotion: The amount of emotion that they feel for their parent changes. Some are flooded with anger or devastation. Others report feeling numb.

Positive or negative affect: The flavor of emotion changes, often becoming more negative as the child becomes more estranged. For example, someone might go from feeling that their mom is difficult to resenting or even hating her.

Desire for reconciliation: The wish to remain in the family changes. Some decide to cut ties. Others hold out hope that the relationship can be repaired if certain parental behaviors change.

Role reciprocity: They no longer think their parents are behaving the way a mom and dad should. And they stop behaving as a child might be expected to toward a parent. For instance, they may refuse to visit when a parent is sick or even dying.

Legal action: They formally sever ties with a parent, like changing their name or beneficiaries in their will.

All of these behaviors occur on a spectrum, and not all are at play in every estrangement, Scharp says. People may also fluctuate, moving closer — or away — from a parent at different times.

If parents understand this, they may be able to improve the relationship. "The continuum is where the compromise can exist," Scharp says.

On Reddit, commenters share strategies on how to pull back from parents: respond to every other call or text; return calls when you know your parents will be busy; request that they stop asking about you; and start "grey rocking," which is to deliberately make your communication as dull and unresponsive as, well, a grey rock.

Yet people who are pulling away don't always tell their parents. Even when they do, parents sometimes resist the boundaries their children are trying to set.

Meanwhile, parents may mistake the pullback as a natural developmental phase, realizing the scope only in hindsight.

"The final cutoff is the undeniable writing on the wall," says Jennifer Hershon, a family-estrangement coach based in Sacramento. "But there's room for repair before the pattern is entrenched."

Joe Bernstein, 51, spent decades trying to set boundaries with his dad after what he described as an adverse childhood. First, he tried talking to his father less. Then when he got married and had a child, he stopped sharing news of his family and refused to allow get-togethers. He also tried to actively put his dad out of his mind.

But none of this made him feel better, Bernstein says. He still had flashbacks about incidents in his childhood. He felt consumed by anger. And the more he pulled away, the more his father pushed back, he says.

Then three years ago, Bernstein started therapy, which helped him process his feelings. When his dad later criticized this, Bernstein says he responded by blocking his father.

"This gives me the quantum of solace to step back and sit more peacefully with the situation," says Bernstein, a higher-education administrator in Chicago. "And it leads to even a sense of compassion for him because he had a rough childhood, too."

As for a potential reconciliation, Bernstein says he would welcome it if his father was able to treat him with respect and civility. "That would be the better outcome," he says. "Because ending things in darkness isn't good for anyone."

What can estranged parents and children do to bridge the divide?

Not all people who have pulled away or cut off a parent may want to reconnect. If they were abused, for example, it may be safer to stay away.

Yet many estrangements are caused by communication or boundary issues. In these instances, therapists recommend parents and kids who want to repair the relationship meet in a neutral setting, like a restaurant, to talk. The adult child should acknowledge that they are pulling away — and focus on patterns, not individual incidents, when they explain what is wrong.

Parents should have a notebook with them, says Catherine Hickem, a psychotherapist in Atlanta who specializes in parent-adult child relationships. She recommends that parents tell their child: "I realize I have made some mistakes that have hurt you and I want to hear about all of them."

It is important for parents not to be defensive, try to explain themselves or justify their actions, Hickem says. They should listen. Tell their child that they appreciate the courage it took to tell the truth. And promise to work to change their behavior.

Then the parent should take a few days to reflect on what they heard, call their child back and keep the dialogue going.

"Repair is not this fully cathartic moment," says Rachel Haack, a licensed marriage and family therapist in Reno, Nev., who works with families dealing with estrangement. "It's staying connected through the distance."

Write to Elizabeth Bernstein at Elizabeth.Bernstein@wsj.com

data.title: Avenue Supermarts Q2 net profit rises 8.5%, revenue up 17.8%
data.description:
Avenue Supermarts, which operates DMart stores, reported an 8.5% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to ₹743.5 crore for the quarter ended 30 September 2026 (Q2 FY27), against ₹685 crore a year earlier, the company said on 10 October 2026.

Consolidated revenue rose 17.8% to ₹19,644 crore from ₹16,676 crore. EBITDA grew 15% to ₹1,394 crore from ₹1,214 crore. The margin was 7%, against 7.3% a year ago.

On a standalone basis, net profit rose 7.6% to ₹803.5 crore from ₹746.5 crore. Revenue grew 18.4% to ₹19,206 crore from ₹16,219 crore, and EBITDA rose 14% to ₹1,403 crore from ₹1,230 crore. The margin was 7%, against 7.6% a year ago. Standalone basic earnings per share (EPS) stood at ₹12.32, against ₹11.47.

For the half year ended 30 September 2026 (H1 FY27), standalone revenue grew 16.8% to ₹37,550 crore. EBITDA rose 15.2% to ₹2,930 crore, and net profit increased 10.3% to ₹1,739 crore. Standalone basic EPS was ₹26.67, against ₹24.22.

Consolidated half-year revenue stood at ₹38,439 crore, against ₹33,036 crore a year earlier. Consolidated EBITDA was ₹2,892 crore, against ₹2,513 crore, and net profit was ₹1,603 crore, against ₹1,458 crore.

Commenting on the DMart brick-and-mortar business, Managing Director and CEO Anshul Asawa said stores that are two years and older grew 9.5% in Q2 FY27, against 6.8% in Q2 FY26. He said the pricing proposition remains strong in an inflationary environment, while wage inflation at entry level has led to a marginal increase in operating expenses.

The company opened 15 new stores during the quarter, taking its total store count to 518. This includes one store at Navi Mumbai that is currently closed for customers due to reconstruction. The company added 18 stores in H1 FY27. As of 30 September 2026, the stores had a retail business area of 21.4 million sq ft.

Vikram Dasu, whole-time director and CEO of Avenue E-Commerce, said on the DMart Ready business that the company is focused on driving greater operational efficiencies and strengthening customer experience in the cities where it currently operates.

On the NSE, Avenue Supermarts shares closed at ₹3,516.80, down ₹68.20, or 1.90%.

data.title: China proposes stricter car design, testing rules, including ban on fully hidden door handles
data.description:
China's industry ministry on Saturday proposed tighter oversight of automakers' innovative designs and research and development testing. It said some manufacturers had rushed out new models without enough validation, which raised safety and environmental risks.

• From January 1, 2027, automakers seeking approval for new models must submit more technical details on innovative designs and testing. Models that are poorly tested or backed by false data will be rejected, the draft said

• Models that already have approval must file information on their innovative designs by July 1, 2027. If they do not and have safety hazards, automakers must halt production and recall them

• The draft bans fully hidden door handles and foldable or flexible displays. It also bars use of "zero-gravity" or swivel seats while driving

• Key functions such as lights and wipers must keep physical controls

• The ministry drafted the rules with three other agencies and is taking public comment until November 10

data.title: Germany sticks to Russia sanctions after Trump announcement on diesel
data.description:
Germany said on Saturday it would maintain sanctions against Russia over its war on Ukraine following US President Donald Trump's announcement that his administration had temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel.

"The federal government has taken note of the US decision relating to Russian diesel deliveries," government spokesperson Stefan Kornelius said in a statement.

He said Germany's position remained clear: "The federal government remains committed to the decisions on sanctions against Russia and is working with its European partners on further sanctions."

He said Germany's support for Ukraine was unchanged and diplomatic efforts to reach a solution would continue.

Trump said on Friday that Russia had agreed to supply diesel to global markets in an effort to lower fuel prices. He said his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for its war on Ukraine.

Prices for diesel, used for agriculture, heating homes and trucking, have risen to near record levels, posing a risk for Trump's fellow Republicans ahead of the November 3 congressional elections that will determine whether they maintain thin control of Congress.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who visited Kyiv last weekend, has said repeatedly that Germany, Ukraine's largest European donor, would not reduce its support for the Kyiv government.

data.title: AAVE Jumps After Citrini Research Bets On DeFi Tokens’ $157T Tokenization Opportunity
data.description:
Key points:
  • Aave rose over 4% on Saturday, the clearest gainer among five DeFi tokens reportedly named in Citrini Research’s tokenization basket, while Bitcoin added only 0.2%.
  • Citrini argued that moving traditional assets onchain could expand trading, lending and payment markets.
  • The firm cautioned that higher onchain volume would not necessarily lift token prices, pointing instead to revenue models, fee allocation and token-holder participation.

Aave (AAVE) edged higher on Saturday, outperforming Bitcoin (BTC) and becoming the clearest gainer among five decentralized finance (DeFi) tokens Citrini Research reportedly named in its tokenization basket this week.

Citrini, an independent financial and thematic investment research firm, published the basket on Thursday, explaining that moving traditional assets onto blockchains could expand on-chain trading, lending and payment markets, according to a CoinDesk report. The scale gap was the starting point for the argument.

Citrini said the question for investors was not whether more assets get tokenized, but “where the economics accrue.” It described an onchain ecosystem that now ran from tokenized treasuries, equities, and options to programmable debt, lending, payments, and yield protocols - “entire financial applications that simply didn’t exist a few years ago.”

Bitcoin Extends Weekly Losses As Ether.fi Slides, Pendle And Uniswap Edge Higher

That distinction was showing up in the prices. While AAVE gained, the rest of the group barely moved. Pendle (PENDLE) gained 0.8%, and Uniswap (UNI) gained 0.3%, both only slightly ahead of Bitcoin, which was up only 0.2% in the last 24 hours. Ether.fi (ETHFI) went the other way, falling 5.5% over the past 24 hours.

Bitcoin’s price fell back to $82,761 at the time of writing. Over the week, Bitcoin has fallen over 2%, despite having reached the $86,000 range just last week.

On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

AAVE Rallies After MetaMask Integration Drives AI Trading Buzz

Aave's gain came as MetaMask's Agent Wallet was integrated with Aave's MCP, connecting the lending protocol to AI-driven transactions. The protocol also reported rising V4 deposits ahead of a deployment review and strong third-quarter growth.

AAVE’s price was up over 4% over the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around AAVE remained in the ‘neutral’ zone, while chatter around it shifted to ‘high’ from ‘normal’ levels over the past day.

What Citrini Named

According to the research firm, global equities were worth over $157 trillion against a crypto market capitalization of nearly $2.66 trillion, the firm said. It added that the on-chain value of tokenized stocks and equities had climbed to roughly $4.84 billion.

Citrini pointed to Robinhood (HOOD) Chain as the first to open the market with stock tokens, and noted that in the week ending Sept. 13, Solana’s (SOL) decentralized exchanges processed about 208 million trades against 190 million on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE). The firm also favored Coinbase (COIN), besides highlighting Hyperliquid (HYPE).

HOOD stock closed up by over 1% on Friday. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around HOOD remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter stayed at ‘normal’ levels over the past day.

Volume Isn't Value

The firm was explicit that none of this guaranteed that the tokens would go up. Higher on-chain volume does not necessarily lift token prices, Citrini said. What mattered more was how a protocol earned revenue, where its fees went, and whether token holders shared in them.

Over a week, the picture was still weak.

Uniswap is down roughly 20% and Pendle 9%, against a 2% decline in Bitcoin.

data.title: RBI may raise repo rate by 75-100 bps in current cycle: Report
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) could raise the repo rate by 75-100 basis points in the current tightening cycle, with inflation expected to remain elevated before easing from the next financial year, according to an SBI Capital Markets report.

SBI Caps said gradual rate increases remain the base case, although a larger hike in December 2026 cannot be ruled out depending on inflation readings for September and October.

The report said the Monetary Policy Committee's 25-basis-point repo rate hike and its shift in stance from "Neutral" to "Calibrated Tightening" signal a stronger focus on containing inflation. It expects the policy cycle to turn around in the first quarter of FY28 as the growth-inflation balance evolves.

Consumer inflation is expected to peak in the third quarter of FY27, while wholesale price inflation could begin easing from March 2027 as favourable base effects set in. Consumer price inflation is likely to trend below 5 per cent year-on-year beyond Q1FY28, the report said.

India's economic growth has remained strong, with real gross domestic product (GDP) expanding 7.8 per cent year-on-year in Q1FY27, exceeding market expectations of 7.1 per cent. Manufacturing grew 9.2 per cent, while gross fixed capital formation rose 11.9 per cent during the quarter.

However, the brokerage flagged risks to consumption in the second half of FY27, including rising borrowing costs, subdued rural sentiment and weaker kharif sowing. It also warned that prolonged geopolitical conflicts and crude oil prices around USD 100 per barrel could sustain cost pressures.

The report noted benchmark 10-year government bond yields had risen around 70 basis points in calendar year 2026, with yields likely to remain elevated until geopolitical tensions ease and inflationary pressures moderate.

Higher interest rates are expected to support bank margins in the near term, although non-food credit growth could gradually slow towards the end of FY27. SBI Capital Markets expects FY27 to remain favourable for banks, while bonds could regain investor interest in FY28.

The report also highlighted global uncertainty, with rising yields in advanced economies and capital outflows from emerging markets adding to financial pressures.

data.title: Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro Demand Is Likely Slipping — But Gene Munster Says That’s Not The Real Story
data.description:
Key points:
  • Munster said iPhone 18 Pro lead times across eight countries initially came in significantly ahead of last year's iPhone 17 Pro, suggesting strong early demand for Apple's latest premium model.
  • However, he noted that the lead times have since fallen considerably further, which are 31% shorter now.
  • Munster acknowledged that the decline is concerning, but said some deterioration was expected because Apple's new iPhone Duo could pull consumers away from the Pro lineup.

Apple Inc.'s (AAPL) iPhone 18 Pro demand may be losing some momentum after a strong start, but Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster believes the latest data needs to be viewed in the broader context of Apple's new iPhone lineup.

Munster pointed to a key distinction between the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max as an early indicator of how consumers are responding to Apple's split product cycle.

Apple shares ended with a loss of over 1% in Friday’s regular trade and edged lower by another 0.2% in the afterhours session.

iPhone 18 Pro Lead Times Are Falling

Munster said iPhone 18 Pro lead times across eight countries initially came in significantly ahead of last year's iPhone 17 Pro, suggesting strong early demand for Apple's latest premium model.

On launch day, iPhone 18 Pro lead times were 15% longer than those for the iPhone 17 Pro a year earlier, he noted. They remained 15% higher after one week before falling to 5% below last year's levels at the two-week mark.

Munster said that the lead times have since fallen considerably further, which are 31% shorter now.

He acknowledged that the decline is concerning, but said some deterioration was expected because Apple's new iPhone Duo could pull consumers away from the Pro lineup.

"Going into the cycle, I predicted we would see lead times 20% lower than last year given the carrot of the new Duo would pull former Pro buyers up to the Duo," he said.

iPhone 18 Pro Max Holds Up Despite The Duo

While the iPhone 18 Pro has seen lead times fall sharply, the Pro Max has held up much better, Munster observed.

On launch day, iPhone 18 Pro Max lead times were 18% longer than the iPhone 17 Pro Max a year earlier. They remained 8% higher after one week and 6% higher after two weeks, he said. Today, they are still roughly in line with last year's levels, according to Munster, who termed this as a “win” for Apple, while noting that he expected the Duo to pull a meaningful portion of last year's Pro Max buyers away from the premium lineup.

"My guess is a sizable, maybe 20%, of last year's early Pro Max buyers are holding off for the Duo," he said.

If that is happening, Munster argues the stable Pro Max lead times could indicate that other iPhone buyers are moving up the product ladder instead.

One possibility is that consumers who would normally buy the standard iPhone 18 are choosing the Pro or Pro Max instead because the standard model will not ship until next spring. "In this case, that's a win for the FY27 iPhone revenue," Munster said.

That potential mix shift could become increasingly important as investors assess whether Apple's decision to split its iPhone launch cycle is actually working. The combined iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max lead times are currently averaging about three weeks, Munster said, which remains roughly in line with last year's combined figure. But he cautioned that the direction of the most recent data matters.

"The trend of the fast decline in recent weeks is more telling," Munster said, while highlighting that the next major test will come when Apple begins taking preorders for the iPhone Duo.

What Retail Traders Think Of AAPL Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Apple trended in the ‘neutral’ territory at the time of writing.

AAPL stock is up 24% year-to-date and 33% over the past 12 months. The S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) is up 16% over the past 12 months, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is up 23%.

data.title: Credit card overlimit facility: Eligibility, charges and 6 factors to consider before opting in
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- A sudden medical bill, surgery, or an unexpected expense can push an individual's credit card spending beyond its approved limit. In such cases, an overlimit facility may help you complete these transactions, but the extra spending can still come at a meaningful cost.

That is why, before opting in, credit cardholders should understand how the facility works, what fees may apply, and how using such a service can affect an individual's credit profile.

It is vital to keep in mind that, as of October 2026, major Indian financial institutions generally charge a credit card overlimit fee of about 2.5% on the amount exceeding the assigned credit limit, subject to a minimum charge of approximately Rs.500- Rs.600, along with applicable GST. This fee may vary by banking institution and credit card variant.

For example, SBI Card sets a minimum fee of Rs.600 for credit card overlimit charges, whereas HDFC Bank, Axis Bank and ICICI Bank specify a minimum of Rs.550, Rs.500 and Rs.500, respectively.

That is why credit cardholders should check their respective banks' latest terms, eligibility requirements (if any) and associated conditions and refer to their official websites for complete details before availing of this facility.

To put it simply, a credit card overlimit facility permits a credit card holder to spend money beyond their assigned credit limit. This spending is permitted subject to the issuer's terms, approval and conditions. For example, if your credit limit is Rs.1 lakh, the facility may permit an eligible transaction that might take your total outstanding balance beyond this amount.

Still, it is essential to keep in mind that this facility is not 'automatic' and the issuer might also decline transactions or impose fines for exceeding the limit, as per their predetermined policies in such cases. This calls for a conceptual understanding of the credit card overlimit facility so that this facility can be utilised meaningfully to the advantage of a credit card holder.

As per the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rules, all card issuers are mandated to obtain clear and explicit consent from the respective credit card holder before extending an overlimit facility. In case the user opts out of this consent, such a facility cannot be extended to them. No fee can be imposed arbitrarily by the credit card issuing institution if the credit card holder did not voluntarily opt for this facility.

If an individual explicitly opts for this service, the terms and conditions of the respective credit card institution will apply. In such cases, banks may levy fees when an individual's outstanding balance exceeds the approved limit, depending primarily on their terms and applicable regulations. To gain complete clarity on this, credit card users should check the latest applicable fees, speak to the customer service team if they have doubts, and check whether charges apply only to the excess amount or on another specified basis.

This is yet another vital aspect that requires due consideration. This means that opting in alone does not guarantee that every transaction above an individual's credit card limit will be approved. Based on the terms, conditions, risk assessment and policies, the credit card issuing institution might still reject or withhold a transaction.

If you opt for the service, utilise funds, and do not repay the outstanding amount in full, this may increase your overall debt. To avoid late surprises, you should carefully review your credit cards' interest-free period rules and repayment terms, rather than simply ignoring these aspects and treating the facility as 'extra income'. In case of doubts, it is wise to first speak to the designated customer service team so that the facility is availed only after a complete understanding.

When you spend beyond your credit card limit, it can increase your credit utilisation ratio. Such a development can adversely affect your credit score. To put it simply, if your total credit limit is Rs.1 lakh, as a general guideline, you should keep your credit utilisation ratio to about 25-30% of this limit, i.e., Rs.25,000 to Rs.30,000. This is because higher utilisation can signal greater dependence on borrowed funds, particularly if it persists.

Finally, the total amount spent above your credit limit must also be repaid in accordance with the stipulations and regulations. Missing the repayment deadline, even delaying it by one day, can result in serious consequences, such as late-payment penalties, and can also decisively alter an individual's credit history.

In summary, a credit card overlimit facility can definitely provide flexibility to individual credit card holders during emergencies. Still, it should not be looked at as a substitute for adequate savings or careful budgeting.

One should consider opting into this service only after acknowledging and understanding the associated charges, interest costs, possible penalties, and long-term ramifications. Using it sparingly to avoid unnecessary debt is a wise way to handle this facility.

data.title: EU's Irish presidency wants 8% cut to proposed 2028-2034 budget plan
data.description:
By Jan Strupczewski and Foo Yun Chee

The European Union's long-term budget for the period 2028 to 2034 should be 8% lower than the European Commission's proposed €2 trillion, the Irish EU presidency said on Saturday.

This would result in a budget of €1.6 trillion, according to the Irish proposal, though it will be subject to contentious negotiations among EU countries in the coming months.

The proposal still marks a 30% increase over the current budget, which runs from 2021 to 2027, and is certain to face stiff resistance from some countries such as Germany that want to keep a firm lid on spending.

The EU budget is the main source of financing for all of the 27-country bloc's main policies.

The Commission, the EU executive, has said the bloc will have to deal with new challenges such as spending more on defence and making Europe more competitive, while some EU countries want to retain most of the expenditure on old policies to support farming and regional development.

"The Negotiating Box provides savings of 8%, or €141 billion, on the Commission's original proposal," said Ireland, current holder of the EU's six-month rotating presidency, referring to its compromise proposal.

Ireland put the Commission's original €2 trillion figure at €1.76 trillion based on 2025 prices, which resulted in an 8% reduction.

The proposal sets out a 3% cut in spending on regional development, agriculture and fisheries spending from the Commission's own figures, and a 13% reduction in spending on competitiveness, prosperity and security.

It foresees €55 billion in new financing options derived from customs duties and selling CO2 emissions permits to companies, among other sources.

EU leaders will discuss the Irish proposal in Brussels on October 15 to 16. The ⁠EU budget, which is known as the Multiannual Financial Framework, needs to be agreed by all 27 member states.

While more frugally-minded countries such as Germany, the Netherlands and the Nordic countries have called for budget cutbacks, others including Spain, Italy and Poland are keen to protect expenditure.
